audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows disagreed with both the packet chart and this page's own whys — Cassiopeia was given levels 1, 2 and 3 while whys[0] and whys[1] say she has no Miasma yet and you land the stun for free, and the first-item row was Skill while whys[5] says your burst one-rotates her before Rylai's.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Riven, Riven, Skill, Riven, Skill, Riven, Cassiopeia] and matches whys[0..6] row for row. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion from Cassiopeia's side: where the shipped chart and the packet disagree, the packet is the one that matches the prose.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 flipped as matched full/content pairs, with ratings raised off 2/10 on the rows that are now Riven's and the phases whys rewritten to justify them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twin Fang's healing was never given an answer, and the R interaction was buried in one late-game sentence.
audit.why: Twin Fang (E, 0.75s cooldown) heals her for a share of the damage it deals to poisoned targets — every chip trade refunds her, which is exactly why extended fights lose. Petrifying Gaze only STUNS enemies facing her; anyone with their back turned is merely slowed, so your approach angle decides whether her ultimate is a death sentence or a slow.
audit.corrected: wants.you[1] now buys Executioner's Calling against Twin Fang. The facing rule was already stated correctly in late and is left as-is.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid and whys[3] both tell you to track 'Miasma's 12-second cooldown'.
audit.why: Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16 — 24 seconds at rank 1, and never lower than 16. The page halved the single most important timer in the lane, which would have you walking up while it is still available.
audit.corrected: Both now state 24 seconds at rank 1, dropping to 16 when maxed.

edits.before: The mid-lane phase is where this matchup gets decided. Track Miasma's 12-second cooldown like a spell timer — the moment it expires is your window to close distance. Use Q resets to approach at an angle rather than a straight line so she cannot simply drop Miasma at your feet. At Level 6, Blade of the Exile extends your threat range enough that Wind Slash can punish her if she kites just outside melee — bait Miasma, dash in with E, Q3-knockup into W-stun, and R-execute if she burns Flash or drops below half HP. Keep Mercs in your back pocket; the grounding plus the magic damage across a long trade is her win condition, not a single nuke.
edits.after: The mid-lane phase is where this matchup gets decided. Miasma is 24 seconds at rank 1 and still 16 when maxed — the moment she spends it is your window to close. Use Q resets to approach at an angle rather than a straight line so she cannot drop it at your feet. At Level 6, Blade of the Exile extends your threat range enough that Wind Slash punishes her if she kites just outside melee — bait Miasma, dash in with E, Q3 knockback into W-stun, and R-execute if she burns Flash or drops below half HP. Keep Mercs in your back pocket; grounding plus magic damage across a long trade is her win condition, not a single nuke.
